about: Code this package copies, one record per upstream file. Each copied Go file keeps its upstream copyright and license header and says what changed.

files.changes: exitStatus, reporting the signal by its name without SIG ("TERM") instead of 128+n. Its process-tree kill (killProcessTree, killDescendants, readProcChildren, lines 760-829) is not used: each run's subreaper guard (guard.go, our own code) ends every descendant.
executionStream as outputStream: the limit is always set, the reader is closed by its owner, and the kept bytes are never nil so they marshal as an empty base64 string.
resolveByteLimit on ints with one maximum, returning the protocol's invalid error instead of a gRPC status.

The credential with supplementary groups, and the environment (PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, then the request's variables over them). No credential when the user is the daemon's own; a switch without CAP_SETUID and CAP_SETGID is refused as denied; no cgroup, no oom/nice shell wrapper, no default variables from a service; Connect errors replaced by the protocol's kinds.
GetUserIdUints unexported; the user may also be a uid[:gid] that /etc/passwd lacks.
expand kept; ExpandAndResolve as resolveCwd with no default workdir, and a missing or non-directory cwd answered as not_found or invalid.

GetEntryInfoWithResolver, getEntryType and getBase as entryOf and typeOf: a symlink is reported as a symlink with its target as written (os.Readlink), not as its target's type; the mode keeps setuid, setgid and sticky from Stat_t; mtime in milliseconds; no access or change times, permission string or xattr metadata.
entryInfo as Stat: Lstat unless follow is asked; uid and gid as numbers, not looked-up names; the protocol's error kinds instead of Connect codes.

ListDir, followSymlink, checkIfDirectory and walkDir as List: the listed directory is followed if it is a symlink and paths keep the asked path; depth from 1 to 16; an offset to page, and a stop at 1000 entries or 768 KiB of JSON with truncated set; an unreadable directory stays listed without its contents; not_dir instead of invalid argument.
Move without a user, without making the destination's parents, and without returning the entry; overwrite and the checks below come from sandboxd.

writeFSError and writeMakeDirectoryError as fsError, with the protocol's kinds (not_found, denied, exists, not_dir, is_dir, unsupported for EXDEV, limit for ENOSPC) instead of HTTP statuses; makeDirectory kept, a directory already there being fine only with parents; handleDeleteFile as Remove with no sandbox root to clear; handleFileAction's move checks (same path, into itself) as Move, replacing as rename(2) does only with overwrite, and otherwise renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE (or a link and unlink of a file where that is missing) instead of a check before the rename; no copy.

extractTar, extractEntry, replaceSymlink and writeViaTemp as functions: the target directory is the root; an entry that is absolute or has a .. part is refused before cleaning; the count of entries written is returned; no gzip, no entry or byte cap, no fsync per file; writeExtractError folded into errors of the protocol's kinds that name the entry (denied for an escape, exists for a type clash, invalid for a bad archive); directories keep owner access while the archive is read and get their archived modes at its end, deepest first, also when they existed.
SanitizePath as sanitizePath on a root already resolved and a relative path, so joinUnderRoot is not needed; a dangling symlink on the way is refused instead of resolved lexically.

ProcessRegistry as Table: ids are "p1", "p2", ... from a counter under the table's lock; processes are kept in start order; at most 256, the one that ended first dropped when a start needs room, a start refused as limit when all run; no SignalAll (init ends every guard).

ManagedProcess as proc: the exit (code, or signal name without SIG) and end time recorded when the guard is done; Signal goes to the program's group through its guard and does nothing once it ended; CloseStdin as process.write's close, refused on a terminal; ResizeTTY refused without a terminal or after the end, with the size set by our own ioctl instead of creack/pty.

WriteStdin, SendSignal and ResizeTTY as Table.Write, Signal and Resize: the protocol's kinds instead of gRPC codes (not_found, invalid, timeout); a write has a 10 s deadline and stops when its call is cancelled; HUP added to the signals.
The signal switch as a map of TERM, INT, KILL and HUP; any other name is invalid.
List over the table in start order, with ended processes kept, argv, pty, running, exit code, signal and start and end times in milliseconds.
The pty read loop, which ends on EIO or EOF, as collect for every stream: bytes go to the stream's ring, not to subscribers; ResizeTty folded into Resize.
